newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: CNPC nearing $1.2 bln Venezuelan orimulsion deal.
newsitem.headline: CNPC nearing $1.2 bln Venezuelan orimulsion deal.

text.p: China National Petroleum Corp (CNPC) plans to sign a $1.2 billion boiler fuel deal with Venezuela's state-owned Bitumenes de Orinoco (BITOR) in October, a source close to the talks said on Thursday.

The state company was also considering a extra-heavy oil venture with Venezuela in the Orinoco oil belt, possibly in a association with Italy's Agip, and a petrochemical deal to produce fertilizers, the source added.

CNPC was very happy with trials of the trademark Orimulsion fuel, used for electricity generation, and the joint-venture would produce 100-120,000 barrels per day (bpd) all for export to China, he added.
CNPC would take a 60 percent share in the joint company.
BITOR, a subsidiary of state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA), exported 4.2 million tonnes of Orimulsion in 1996 and hopes to produce 20 million tonnes by the end of the decade.
The deal would represent a deepening of China's business interests in Venezuela where it recently won two contracts to exploit mature oilfields on behalf of PDVSA.
CNPC signed the contracts, for which it paid $358 million, on Tuesday and the source expected these to generate 200,000 bpd of crude production within the next few years.

CNPC was also awaiting the results of Venezuela's petrochemical privatization with interest, with a view to setting up an ammonia or urea joint-venture for supply to its huge fertilizer market, he said.
